question_text: Express −1 − i√3 in the modulus-amplitude form.

mark_split.label: Find the amplitude θ from the quadrant and write r(cos θ + i sin θ)

recall_prompt: Say how you would write a complex number in modulus-amplitude form — what two numbers you need and how the quadrant fixes the angle.
insider_note: tan θ = √3 also fits π/3, the first-quadrant point (1, √3) — the quadrant sentence is what separates the two and carries the second mark. (−1, −√3) is in the third quadrant, so θ = −π + π/3 = −2π/3.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find r
steps.margin_note: First mark. x = −1, y = −√3, so r = √(1 + 3) = 2.

recall.must_convey: That x = −1, y = −√3 and the modulus r = √(1 + 3) = 2.
accept: x is minus one, y is minus root three, r is root of one plus three which is two
the modulus is root four equals two
r equals root x squared plus y squared, that is two
one plus three is four, root of that is two

steps.why: Both coordinates are negative, but both square to positive numbers, so r = 2 exactly as for 1 + i√3. The two signs return in the next step to put the point in the third quadrant.
common_mistakes: Taking r negative because both coordinates are negative.

steps.label: Find θ and write the form
steps.margin_note: Second mark. tan θ = √3, but (−1, −√3) is in the THIRD quadrant, so the principal amplitude is θ = −π + π/3 = −2π/3. Check: 2 cos(−2π/3) = −1 and 2 sin(−2π/3) = −√3.

recall.must_convey: That tan θ = √3 with the point in the third quadrant gives the principal amplitude θ = −2π/3, so the form is 2(cos(−2π/3) + i sin(−2π/3)) = 2(cos 2π/3 − i sin 2π/3).
accept: tan theta is root three but the point is in the third quadrant so theta is minus two pi by three
the form is two times cos minus two pi by three plus i sin minus two pi by three
third quadrant, theta equals minus pi plus pi by three equals minus two pi by three
point third quadrant lo undi kabatti theta minus two pi by three
two times cos two pi by three minus i sin two pi by three

steps.why: tan θ = √3 is true for π/3 (first quadrant) and −2π/3 (third quadrant). The point has both coordinates negative, so it is in the third, and the principal amplitude in (−π, π] is −2π/3. Since cos is even and sin is odd, this is the same as 2(cos 2π/3 − i sin 2π/3).
common_mistakes: Taking θ = π/3 straight from tan θ = √3 — that is the point (1, √3).
Writing 2(cos 2π/3 + i sin 2π/3), which is −1 + i√3.
